articles.title: IN BRIEF: Putin speaks on Russia’s economic sustainability, Europe’s aggression
articles.body:
MOSCOW, October 2. /TASS/. Despite the existing problems, Russia continues to develop, and its economy remains healthy and sustainable, Russian President Vladimir Putin told the plenary session of the 23rd Valdai International Discussion Club.
He also said that Russia’s offensive in the special military operation zone is gaining momentum, and that Europe’s aggressive attitude towards Russia is aimed at diverting attention from domestic economic failures.
Below are the Russian leader’s key remarks.
Russia’s sustainability and way to future
Russia is ready to forge its path to the future with realistic assessment of risks, opportunities and necessary goals, "and, of course, it is ready to engage in such efforts jointly with other countries and peoples."
"We do have some difficulties, but we are resolving them. Macroeconomic indices show that our economy is healthy, and that our financial system and economic institutions are working in a sustainable manner."
Russia’s economy has certain problems and issues that need to be solved, but "who does not?" "Look at any other region of the world. Everyone has its own problems."
Russia had inflation problems: "We jump-started the economy, we overheated it. And we made a deliberate choice to cool it down. We did it deliberately, being perfectly aware that if the Central Bank raises the key rate, investment will decline. It was obvious to everyone, and it did lead to such consequences. What matters now is to make sure that we don’t overcool the economy."
This year, inflation nearly halved compared to 2025. "This year’s budget deficit is around three percent. I’m sure that next year it will be two."
Situation in special operation zone
The situation in the special operation zone is gaining momentum, with over 1,300 square kilometers of territory taken under Russia’s control in September alone. "This is 2.5 times higher than in the previous months."
The government of Ukraine and the European Union claim they will be able to hold the remaining 11% of Donbass’s territory over the next year and a half or two. "We believe that it will happen way sooner, given the pace of our advance, which, as I have just mentioned, is accelerating."
For Russia, the situation around Ukraine is not a question of land, it’s a question of people. "It’s not about a piece of territory, it’s about people. The point is that we need to create conditions not for a temporary truce, but for a lasting peace. And we need security guarantees for that."
It is necessary to strive for peace agreements on Ukraine: "If they [Western countries and Ukraine] agree to terms that Russia also finds acceptable, it will be better to put an end to these sad events and avoid additional casualties on both sides."
Russia is ready to launch and complete negotiations on Ukraine as promptly as possible, but, "naturally, on conditions that the Russian Federation and its people find acceptable."
"However, it appears that the other side simply does not want to end the hostilities."
Russia’s response
Kiev troops started to strike Russian cargo ships in the Black Sea, and Russia had to respond: "Well, we gave our answer. And now they are asking us to stop via all channels. But they [the Kiev government] were the ones to start this."
"They started attacking our refineries, openly declaring that their objective is to harm our economy. They attained their goal to a certain extent because, according to our estimates, we lost about 1% of our GDP. They deliberately started striking civilian targets. Well, they got a tit-for-tat response."
The Russian armed forces started delivering strikes on sites that are crucial for the Ukrainian economy: "Now, by their own admission, they effectively have no metallurgical industry left."
Europe’s aggression
At this point Europe’s leading countries "are much more hostile towards Russia than the United States."
While the United States "is seeking to end the conflict," many European countries, "have now perhaps become the ‘instigators’ of aggressive attitude toward Russia, creating additional crises between Russia and Europe." They are "driven by the unfavorable situation in their own economies, and, consequently, by the unfavorable situation for the ruling elites, combined with shifting political moods."
European politicians want "to justify the need of preparations for war, and to mobilize as many supporters around themselves as possible in order to remain in power." "The logic is very simple, and I’m sure that this constitutes a significant portion of the reasoning behind Europe’s behavior towards the Russian Federation."
"We are not threatening anyone, and we have no intention of attacking anyone, neither in 2029, nor in 2030, nor in 2050. However, if we face aggression, we will be forced to respond. European citizens should clearly understand this and distinguish between our position and the stance taken by certain political leaders in their countries."
The continuous stoking of rhetoric by many European countries is driven by the serious worsening of their domestic economic and political situation. "Look at what is happening in the economy, look what is happening in the social sphere and the quality of life in major European countries. In this situation, they have to shift the focus of their citizens’ attention from domestic issues to outside problems."
"We have no preconditions for resuming and restoring relations with Europe in general or with particular countries."
EU countries "will collapse on their own" because they continue to make mistakes that negatively impact their own economies. "But this is none of our business. We are not interfering."
Weapons as competitive advantage
Russia understands that in case of a direct attack by NATO, it will have to face "an adversary more than twice our size in terms of numbers." "They have huge economic potential, huge military potential. Indeed, our forces and assets would not be that extensive to counter such a threat. And we will have to use our competitive advantages in this struggle."
One of Russia’s main competitive advantages are its strike capabilities. "Yes, of course, France and the United Kingdom are nuclear powers. We understand that, and we are fully aware of that. However, no one else possesses the strike capabilities that Russia has today. And this is our competitive advantage."
"We are not threatening anyone. We simply make it clear that our tools to defend ourselves are not that numerous."
Russia has advanced new weapons systems: "We have new, modern capabilities, including entirely new missile defense penetration systems, advanced medium-range weapons, and state-of-the-art systems that other nations do not possess yet."
"All nuclear powers are highly technologically advanced countries. They will have it at some point in the future. But now they don’t, only we do."
While building new facilities, Russia is taking modern methods of warfare into account: "I assure you, we are currently considering this, and, when we build new enterprises in this sector, we are taking modern methods of warfare into account and do everything possible to ensure they are located in the safest areas possible." "Construction is under way."
Relations with US
Factors marring and damaging Russia-US relations have developed over decades: "We would very much like to see these divisive factors to become a thing of the past, allowing new prospects for mutually beneficial cooperation to emerge."
Russia has proposed and continues to propose to the United States to resume dialogue on strategic arms limitations: "We don not mind resuming this dialogue; we have never been against it. We have offered it, and we are offering it now. There is no answer. Well, if there is no answer, then so be it."
It was Washington that withdrew from agreements curbing the arms race and the proliferation of nuclear weapons: "We were not the ones to walk out of these treaties. The United States did it, under this or that pretext."
"I have quite good, long-standing relations with President (of the US Donald - TASS) Trump. I’m thankful for his efforts to resolve the Ukrainian crisis, and, as I’ve said many times, he is doing it in good faith. And I’m thankful for that, too."
Partnership with China
Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping understand each other without words or interpreters: "You know, what is interesting. It only took one word from him or me, and without interpreters - and without knowing each other's languages - we understood each other instantly."
China never seeks to resolve emerging problems and issues through pressure or military force. This is alien to its philosophy, which is fundamentally rooted in pursuing solutions through peaceful means. For its part, Russia recognizes Beijing's approach, shares this perspective, and notes the strong outcomes generated by the joint efforts of Moscow and Beijing.
"Can China play any role [in promoting peace] at this point? Of course it can. And, first of all, this stems from its growing economic and military potential, from its readiness to expand the zone of free cooperation, and this is what Chinese President Xi Jinping’s initiative ‘One belt, One Road’ is aimed at."
"Together with China, we are developing this initiative, aligning it with Russia's respective projects, including the Greater Eurasian Partnership. We are working jointly, and this is yielding strong, positive results."
Moscow and Beijing will undoubtedly establish a joint framework to actively utilize the Northern Sea Route (NSR) to serve the interests of Russia and China.
Indian premier and peace initiatives
The diversity and unity of Indian culture are highly admirable: "There is something about Indian culture that possesses such uniqueness - a distinctiveness and unity at the same time - that it undoubtedly serves as an exemplary model. This, of course, deserves to be an example."
At every meeting, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi raises the question of resolving the conflict in Ukraine: "He comes up with very good ideas, aimed at searching for mutually acceptable - specifically mutually acceptable - solutions."
The head of the Indian government has a neutral stance, which is nevertheless aimed at bringing the conflict to an end: "By the way, we are grateful to the Indian premier for his desire to resolve this conflict peacefully, and as quickly as possible."
Multipolarity and BRICS
The world should be multipolar; it cannot be bipolar: "It should take into account the interests of all participants of international relations. And, as we have said many times, there is the cornerstone, basic principle: the security of one nation cannot be achieved at the expense of the security of others. This is one of the cornerstones that we believe should form the foundation of the future world order."
"We cannot say exactly how this world will look like. <...> But we need to strive to jointly determine <…> the pillars of the future world order. And this needs to be done without any preconditions."
"An organization such as BRICS may certainly become the prototype for building the future world order."
At this point, BRICS represents nearly half of the planet’s entire population, and its share in the global economy is constantly growing. "This is happening every year, and we can see it in the statistics. And, most importantly, the principles of BRICS' formation and functioning stipulate that everyone is equal. There is no domination of any kind there, and this is what makes it so attractive."
So far, it is hard to say what role BRICS will play in the new architecture of international relations, but it can already be said with certainty that it is "a useful mechanism."

articles.title: Ukraine prepares sanctions on 20-plus Russian oligarchs in response to EU delistings
articles.body:
Ukraine prepares sanctions on 20-plus Russian oligarchs in response to EU delistings
Ukraine is planning to sanction more than 20 Russian oligarchs in response to the European Union's decision to remove billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Oct. 1.
The list has already been approved by President Volodymyr Zelensky and is being formalized, Sybiha told journalists, describing the move as an "asymmetric response" to the EU decision.
"We fought until the last moment, both publicly and privately, to prevent this from happening," Sybiha said. "You removed two oligarchs, and we will add twenty."
According to Sybiha, Canada has already confirmed to Kyiv that it does not plan to lift its own sanctions against Usmanov and Fridman. Ukraine is also working with the U.K., Japan, Australia, and other partners to ensure the two oligarchs remain sanctioned by other countries.
The EU had removed the two oligarchs from its sanctions list on Sept. 22 as part of a compromise to extend the bloc's broader individual sanctions regime for 36 months. The measures had previously been renewed every six months, requiring recurring unanimous agreement among EU member states.
The longer extension reduces the frequency of politically challenging renewal negotiations, during which in the past individual member states have exerted pressure for specific names to be removed from the list.
France had pushed for Usmanov's removal, while Slovakia was also involved in negotiations, and Latvia agreed to allow the delisting of Usmanov and Fridman in order to prevent the sanctions regime from lapsing completely.
Usmanov, who controls mining and steel giant Metalloinvest, and Fridman, founder of the Alfa Group conglomerate, are among Russia's wealthiest businessmen. Both were sanctioned by the EU following Russia's full-scale invasion over their alleged ties to the Kremlin.

articles.title: Jewish groups hail California law making it the first state to list ‘Jewish’ as an ethnicity
articles.body:
California is now the first state in the nation to deem “Jewish” an ethnic and racial identity, rather than just a religious affiliation.
Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom on Wednesday signed SB 1387, a bill that expands California’s legal definition of ethnicity “to include Jewish identity” in demographic data collection. As of Jan. 1, 2029, forms distributed by public entities like schools and prisons will need to include a “Jewish” category when asking for voluntary disclosures of ethnicity or race.
David Bocarsly, CEO of Jewish California, a group that lobbies on behalf of a number of Jewish organizations in the state, described the signing in a statement as “a historic step for the Jewish community.”
“Under the shadow of Nazi race theory, American Jewish leaders asked the government to count us only as a religion,” he said, noting that this approach “didn’t work” and led to exclusion from data that shapes policy.
“Now hate crime, health, poverty, and education data will reflect who Jewish Californians actually are so we can ensure the best support for our community,” Bocarsly added. “Most importantly, it allows us to be seen as the diverse, complex people we are.”
The legislation was a priority among many Jewish groups across the Gold Rush state, who believe that Jewish peoplehood should be connected to more than just religion — and that the law should reflect this relationship.
Newsom expresses reservations over law
Newsom, however, expressed some reservations in signing the bill into law.
“I strongly support this bill’s goal: accurate data leads to better understanding to inform policy,” Newsom, who is considering a presidential run in 2028, wrote in a signing statement. But he said he was concerned that the bill’s strictures would make it hard for state agencies to comply with the new law and with federal laws, and recommended revisiting the bill.
In addition to signing SB 1387 on Wednesday — the final day on which he could approve or veto bills in this year’s legislative session — Newsom also authorized AB 395, which will prohibit public meetings and graduations from being scheduled on major cultural and religious holidays.
“Californians of all faiths and backgrounds should be able to fully participate in public life,” the bill’s author, Democratic Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel, said in a statement.
“For too long members of our religious communities have been forced to choose between observing their faith and participating in important public events and academic milestones,” added Gabriel, who chairs the California Legislative Jewish Caucus.
Newsom approves seveal bills relevant to Jewish community
Also on Wednesday, Newsom approved AB 1763, which will include religious holiday observance as a type of excused absence in schools without requiring a written request from a parent or guardian.
Newsom signed other bills relevant to the Jewish community in the past few days, including AB 2664, which will establish 100-foot protective zones around entrances to houses of worship.
Another new law is AB 1836, which will close a gap in California’s nonprofit security grant structure by extending funds to off-site religious events like Hanukkah menorah lightings. The governor also approved AB 1853, enacting a ban on including misleading or threatening information, like hate speech, in California voter guides.

articles.title: Hundreds protest controversial antisemitism bill in Italy
articles.body:
Barış Seçkin
02 October 2026•Update: 02 October 2026
Hundreds of people rallied in Milan on Thursday against a controversial antisemitism bill under consideration in Italy’s parliament, with Jewish groups joining calls to reject the legislation.
The bill, known as DDL 1004, was introduced by the far-right League party, a junior partner in Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s right-wing coalition government.
It would use criteria adopted by the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) to define antisemitism. After passing the Senate in March, it is now before the Chamber of Deputies for final approval.
Demonstrators gathered outside the renowned La Scala Opera House, waving Palestinian flags, ringing bells and blowing whistles.
They held signs saying “No to the antisemitism bill,” “Criticizing Israel is not antisemitism” and “Protest is a right” while chanting “Free Palestine.” Some unfurled a large banner saying “One voice. No to Bill 1004.”
Speakers at the rally described the bill as dangerous, arguing that it equates criticism of Israel with racial hatred and could silence those criticizing the occupation and discrimination imposed on Palestinians.
Giulia, a member of the Jewish Anti-Racist Laboratory, told Anadolu that her group and other Jewish organizations oppose the bill, noting that Italy already has legislation against hate crimes, racism, discrimination and fascist propaganda under the 1993 Mancino law.
“We do not need a specific law based on the IHRA definition that treats criticism of Israel as antisemitism. We believe this law will increase antisemitism rather than prevent it, because it will silence dissent and solidarity with Palestine,” she said.
“We Jews can play a role by saying that this kind of legislation makes us feel less safe and leads us to believe that antisemitism will increase,” she added.
Bulgarian-born Italian Jewish artist Moni Ovadia also voiced strong opposition.
“This legislation persecutes Jews as well as people who are just and free. I will only say this: If Albert Einstein and Sigmund Freud were alive today, they would be convicted under this law. So would (German-American historian and philosopher) Hannah Arendt,” he said.
Another protest against the bill is scheduled to take place outside the Chamber of Deputies in Rome on Friday.

articles.title: South-east Australia lashed by storms, as Melbourne records wettest day in years
articles.body:
In brief
- South-east Australia has been drenched with heavy rain and lashed by storms.
- Melbourne recorded its wettest day in more than two years, and the SES received hundreds of calls.
Significant rainfall is expected to continue across much of a state that's already been battered by storms and flash flooding.
Melbourne recorded one of its wettest October days in several years after the city received up to 25mm of rain within an hour on Thursday afternoon, with other areas of Victoria also hard hit.
More than 200 calls for help were made to the SES, including six water rescues, after parts of Melbourne were hit by the flash flooding.
The city was plunged into darkness about 3pm as the system moved through, with Melbourne Olympic Park recording 47.8mm of rain since 9am on Thursday.
Bureau of Meteorology senior meteorologist David Crock said the total marked the city's highest daily rainfall total since April 2024.

"[It was] a very wet day for the Melbourne metro area, particularly in the afternoon when that heavy rain moved through," he said on Friday morning.
"That caused a lot of a lot of water all through the suburbs. Some flash flooding in the creeks and a lot of water under bridges."
Rainfall totals of 20-50mm around Ballarat and Melbourne were also recorded on Thursday afternoon, Crock confirmed.
South Australia also recorded significant rainfall, with 20-25mm falling across parts of the Adelaide Hills in the past 24 hours.
Emergency crews were kept busy overnight, with 200 requests for help — 71 were for building damage, 50 for flooding and 44 for trees downs.
"We have assisted Victoria Police with six water rescues, vehicles getting into trouble due to entering flood water or driving in roads that had water catching due to the rainfall that fell pretty quickly in a short period of time," the state emergency service's duty officer Jessie Schleibs told the Australian Associated Press on Friday.
"It's one of the wettest October days we've had in several years."
The busiest units included Barwon South West and metro Melbourne areas, although attention will now move to north-eastern suburbs along with Gippsland.
Rainfall will continue on Friday and Saturday in Victoria, with a flood watch current for catchments across much of central and eastern parts of the state.
"There is much more to come," Crock said.
"We're expecting more rain through Friday and Saturday. Some spots in eastern Victoria could see 100 to 150mm over the next few days.
"Conditions are expected to ease on Sunday as the low pressure system moves off offshore. So conditions will ease from the west.
"Melbourne and Sydney and Canberra and Adelaide should see mostly dry conditions by Sunday."

articles.title: 'Where are they in your film?': Oct. 7 survivor who lost husband, son confronts 'NAZA' directors
articles.body:
A confrontation broke out Thursday evening during a screening of the film NAZA in the Dutch city of Delft after the wife and mother of two Israelis murdered by Hamas during the October 7 massacre confronted the film’s directors, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor.
“Look me in the eyes," Sabine Taasa urged Abraham and Szor. "You’re talking about collateral damage? My husband and my son were murdered by Hamas. Where does this appear in your film?”
Taasa's husband, Gil, and one of her sons, Or, were murdered during the massacre. Additional children of hers were also wounded in the attack. She traveled to the screening in the Netherlands with members of Ad Kan, intending to protest the way the war is portrayed in the film and to share her family’s story with the audience.
"I came here to tell my story. My name is Sabine Tassa. I came from Israel to tell you the truth," she said.
According to footage shared by the Israeli organization Ad Kan, several audience members responded by shouting, “We don’t care,” “Shame on you,” and “We don’t want to hear.”
Dutch Party for Freedom founder and leader Geert Wilders slammed the audience members in a post to X/Twitter responding to the incident.
"The callousness is staggering," Wilders wrote. "Sabine Taasa survived the October 7 massacre. Her 17-year-old son was murdered at Zikim Beach. Her husband was killed shielding their two young sons from a grenade."
“'We don’t care.' That is their answer to her suffering."
"The truth means nothing to the Left. Its alliance with Islam is an expression of moral bankruptcy that threatens the future of the Netherlands and of our civilisation. A crowd can drown out a voice. Not the TRUTH," said Wilders.
In a later post, Wilders stated he hosted Taasa at the Dutch Parliament.
"Her 17-year-old son and her husband were killed. She is a strong and wise Israeli friend," he said. "I will always support Israel and fight Islamic terrorism. Never surrender."
What is 'NAZA'?
NAZA focuses on the war in the Gaza Strip and the harm caused to the Palestinian population during the conflict. The film has drawn criticism in Israel over the way it portrays the war and the actions of the IDF, including the attention it gives to the October 7 massacre and Hamas’s actions.
The protest in the Netherlands focused specifically on this issue, with Taasa demanding that the filmmakers also address the killing of her family members.
Ad Kan attempted to show Oct. 7 atrocity film at showing
At the start of the screening, Ad Kan CEO Avichai Shorshan, who had accompanied Taasa on her trip to the Netherlands, attempted to use a portable projector to show the atrocity film documenting the October 7 massacre on the cinema screen.
According to the organization, audience members tried to stop the screening from continuing, and a confrontation broke out at the venue.
Shorshan criticized the film following the event. “The collateral damage to the State of Israel as a result of the false film is inconceivable,” he said. “This brainwashing can be corrected only through a swift effort to expose the false witnesses and confront them with the truth.”
“We will not accept the spread of antisemitism in Europe; we will continue to fight,” he added.
